chapter: Back in Houston, Club Ebony and Boo Pleasant
title: What became of Boo Pleasant and her children
summary: Boo left the band, fell into a bad crowd, and Cobb and his wife had tried to help raise her children; her son was shot in a park and later died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Boo had an accident in Los Angeles -- not Los Angeles but California, wherever she was, but she left me before I come back here, and she got into an environmental situation that was no good. But when you're young and get weak --
And those kids, what a shame.
I had her in Houston since then, here that I brought her here, a couple three years ago, and she got in with the wrong group here, so I just dropped my hand.
Oh, isn't that a shame? I mean when you've got talent, what an awful pity, isn't it?
Well, Helen, only thing I can say to you, it's hard enough raising the one I got. I can't raise everybody's kids.

I can advise and suggest, be a father to them in my little way, but I've got too many other things to do than to try to raise somebody else's kids. And God knows I tried to do the best I could. She stayed with us and everything so I could get to see her get -- stayed in Jersey with us, trying to save her money. We got her kids, she brought her son in, Ollie, and we had both of her kids and her too at the house. So how far can you go?
Well, you couldn't do more than that.

All right. Everything happened to her bad. Her son was in the park, and he was -- said something to a guy about saying something out of line to his girlfriend, and they thought it was over with, and the guy come later on and had a gun in a paper bag and shot him and put him -- in the spine and crippled him, and he eventually died, had some problems (inaudible).
